title: Families
about: Collocations for talking about families: types of family and relatives (a nuclear family, distant relatives, a close-knit family, a broken home), marriage and divorce (a late husband, a trial separation, a bitter divorce), and having and bringing up children (start a family, expect a baby, provide for your family).

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a nuclear family · opposite: an extended family
items.meaning: a family of just parents and their children, living together
items.example: When my parents were young, a **nuclear family** with two kids and a car was what everyone wanted.
more: Sociologists say the **nuclear family** became common when people moved to cities to find work.
A **nuclear family** that moves abroad often has no grandparents nearby to help with the kids.
items.watchOut: Не atomic family і не core family: «ядро» тут — nuclear. Вимова: /ˈnjuːkliə/, а не «нуклеар».

items.pattern: adjective + noun: an extended family · your extended family
items.meaning: the whole network of relatives: grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins and so on
items.example: We only see our **extended family** at weddings, funerals and big birthdays.
more: My **extended family** has a group chat with forty-three people in it.
When Dad lost his job, our **extended family** helped us a lot.
items.watchOut: Не wide family. A big / large family — це сім'я, де багато дітей (багатодітна), а extended family — уся рідня: дідусі й бабусі, тітки, дядьки, двоюрідні.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a close relative / relation · close relatives · opposite: distant relatives
items.meaning: a member of your nearest family, such as a parent, child, brother or sister
items.example: Doctors usually ask if any **close relatives** have had heart problems.
more: Only **close relatives** can collect the documents for her.
Is he a **close relative** of yours? You look very alike.
items.watchOut: Родич — relative або relation, а не native: native — це носій мови чи корінний житель. «Рідний брат» — просто my brother.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a distant relative / cousin / relation · be distantly related
items.meaning: someone in your family who is not closely related to you, e.g. a cousin of your grandparents
items.example: My surname is rare, so anyone who has it is probably a **distant relative**.
more: She found a **distant cousin** in Brazil through a DNA test.
Apparently we're **distantly related** to a famous poet, but nobody knows exactly how.
items.watchOut: Далекий родич — distant relative, а не far relative. І distant тут — про спорідненість, а не про відстань: родич, який живе далеко, — a relative who lives far away.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a second cousin · a (first) cousin · a third cousin
items.meaning: the child of your mother's or father's cousin
items.example: My **second cousin** Marta and I only met last year, but we get on really well.
more: Half the village are my **second cousins**, so I have to be polite to everyone.
Is she your cousin? — Not exactly, she's a **second cousin**: our mums are cousins.
items.watchOut: Рахунок зсунутий на одиницю: двоюрідний брат чи сестра — (first) cousin, троюрідний — second cousin, а не third cousin. Cousin — і брат, і сестра.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: your close / immediate family (uncountable) · members of your immediate family
items.meaning: your nearest relatives: parents, children, brothers and sisters, husband or wife
items.example: The form asks for the names of everyone in your **immediate family**.
more: My **close family** is small: just my dad, my brother and me.
My **immediate family** all live within ten minutes of each other.
items.watchOut: «Найближча родина» — immediate або close family, а не nearest family. Family тут незлічуване: I've got very little close family, а не very few close families.

items.pattern: noun + noun: a blood relative / relation · related by blood · opposite: related by marriage
items.meaning: a person who is related to you by birth, not by marriage or adoption
items.example: My stepdad isn't a **blood relative**, but he's the only father I've ever known.
more: He left his money to his friends rather than to his **blood relatives**.
Is Anna a **blood relative**, or is she related to you by marriage?
items.watchOut: Родичі чоловіка або дружини (свекор, свекруха, тесть, теща) — in-laws, а не blood relatives. Blood relative і blood relation означають одне й те саме.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a (very) close / close-knit / tight-knit family · be close to sb
items.meaning: a family whose members love, help and support each other a lot
items.example: We're a **close-knit family**, so when Dad was ill, everyone took turns to sit with him.
more: I've always been very **close** to my older sister.
In small villages, families tend to be quite **close-knit**.
items.watchOut: «Дружна сім'я» — a close або close-knit family. A friendly family — привітні до інших люди, це не про зв'язок між собою. «Ми з братом дуже близькі» — We're very close, а не very near.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a loving family / home / parents / marriage
items.meaning: a family where people show their love and care for each other
items.example: Mia grew up in a **loving family**, so she finds it easy to show her feelings.
more: Our old dog has finally found a **loving** home with a family in the village.
Thanks to her **loving parents**, she never felt alone, even in hard times.
items.watchOut: Любляча — loving, а не loved і не lovely: a lovely family — славна, приємна сім'я (так кажуть про враження від людей), а a loving family — сім'я, де одне одного люблять.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a respectable family / job / neighbourhood · come from a respectable family
items.meaning: a family that people see as decent, honest and socially acceptable
items.example: When she brought her boyfriend home, Gran asked straight away whether he came from a **respectable family**.
more: He put on his only suit to look **respectable** at the interview.
They live in a quiet, **respectable** neighbourhood near the park.
items.watchOut: Respectable — порядний, пристойний в очах людей. Respectful — шанобливий, той, хто сам виявляє повагу: respectful children. І respectable — не обов'язково «заможний», як «респектабельний» в українській.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a dysfunctional family / relationship
items.meaning: a family where relationships are unhealthy and people often make each other unhappy
items.example: Many comedians say they grew up in a **dysfunctional family** and learned to make people laugh to survive.
more: Christmas with my **dysfunctional family** usually ends in an argument about money.
The novel shows how one big secret can turn a happy home into a **dysfunctional** one.
items.watchOut: Наголос на другому складі: dys-FUNC-tional. «Неблагополучна сім'я» — dysfunctional, коли проблема у стосунках; deprived, коли бракує грошей і нормальних умов.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: sb's late husband / wife / father · the late Mr X · only before the noun
items.meaning: who has died (a polite way to talk about someone who is dead)
items.example: This was my **late husband**'s favourite chair, and nobody else sits in it.
more: Her **late father** was a well-known doctor in the town.
My grandfather often talks about his **late wife** and how they met at a dance.
items.watchOut: Late тут — «покійний», а не «пізній». Стоїть лише перед іменником: my late wife. He is late — це «він запізнюється»! Dead husband звучить різко; ввічливо — late.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: sb's estranged husband / wife · be estranged from sb · formal
items.meaning: still married, but living apart and on bad terms
items.uk: чоловік (дружина), з яким (якою) живуть окремо й не ладнають, але ще не розлучені
items.example: The singer was seen at the airport with his **estranged wife**, and fans hoped they might get back together.
more: After the argument about the will, the two brothers were **estranged** for ten years.
Her **estranged husband** still pays for the children's school.
items.watchOut: Estranged — не «дивний» (strange). Про подружжя — ще не розлучені, але живуть окремо. Можна і про інших родичів: be estranged from your father — роками не спілкуватися з батьком.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: have / agree to a trial separation
items.meaning: a period when a married couple live apart to decide whether to end their marriage
items.uk: тимчасове роздільне проживання подружжя (на пробу, перш ніж вирішити, чи розлучатися)
items.example: After twenty years of marriage, my aunt and uncle are having a **trial separation**.
more: During their **trial separation**, they still met every Sunday to take the kids to the park.
He's staying at his brother's flat during the **trial separation**.
items.watchOut: «Пожити окремо на пробу» — trial separation, а не test чи probe separation. Trial тут — «випробувальний», як у a trial period, a free trial.

items.pattern: verb + noun: get a divorce · get divorced (from sb) · divorce sb · ask for / file for a divorce
items.meaning: end a marriage officially, by law
items.example: They **got a divorce** after fifteen years, but they still have dinner together on the kids' birthdays.
more: My parents **got divorced** when I was five.
If she really wants a **divorce**, he won't try to stop her.
items.watchOut: «Розлучитися» — get divorced / get a divorce, а не make a divorce. «Розлучитися з ним» — divorce him або get divorced from him, без with.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a bitter / acrimonious (formal) divorce · also a messy divorce
items.meaning: a divorce full of anger, arguments and bad feeling
items.example: After their **bitter divorce**, the couple only talked to each other through lawyers.
more: Their **acrimonious divorce** made family gatherings very awkward for years.
She didn't want a **bitter divorce**, so she let him keep the car.
items.watchOut: Bitter тут — «сповнений злості й образи», а не «гіркий» на смак. «Важке розлучення» — не heavy divorce: кажуть bitter, messy або difficult divorce. Acrimonious — книжне слово.

items.pattern: ex- + noun: sb's ex-husband / ex-wife · informal: my ex · more formal: former husband / wife
items.meaning: the man or woman you used to be married to
items.example: Luckily, Mia gets on well with her **ex-husband**, so the kids can see both parents.
more: I don't really talk about my **ex**; that's all in the past.
Her **ex-husband** has remarried and moved to Canada.
items.watchOut: «Колишня дружина» — ex-wife або former wife, а не past wife. My last wife — «моя попередня (з кількох) дружина», так кажуть, коли шлюбів було кілька.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: come from / grow up in a broken home
items.meaning: a family where the parents have separated or divorced
items.example: He **comes from a broken home**, but his mum and grandparents gave him a happy childhood.
more: Both of my parents grew up in **broken homes**, so they really wanted our family to stay together.
The film is about a boy from a **broken home** who finds a second family in his football team.
items.watchOut: «Неповна сім'я» — a broken home або a single-parent family, а не incomplete family. Broken home звучить трохи старомодно й негативно; нейтральніше — a single-parent family.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a stable home / family / background / relationship
items.meaning: a family where life is calm and secure and nothing changes suddenly
items.example: My parents worked hard to give us a **stable home**, even when money was tight.
more: Moving house six times in five years didn't give the kids a very **stable** home life.
Grandma says a **stable home** matters more than a big house.
items.watchOut: «Благополучна сім'я» — a stable (або happy, secure) home. Prosperous — заможний, це про гроші, а не про спокій у родині.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a deprived home / area / childhood · be deprived of sth
items.meaning: a home without enough money, food or decent living conditions
items.example: She grew up in a **deprived home** in the 1950s, where six people shared two rooms.
more: The government promised more money for **deprived** areas in the north.
Many of the volunteers had a **deprived** childhood themselves.
items.watchOut: Не плутай deprived (бідний, позбавлений необхідного) і depraved (морально зіпсований, розбещений) — різниця в одній літері.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a confirmed bachelor · often humorous
items.meaning: a man who seems to have decided never to marry
items.example: My brother says he's a **confirmed bachelor**, but he's been with the same girlfriend for ten years.
more: Everyone at work thinks of Martin as a **confirmed bachelor**: he lives alone with his cat and likes it that way.
Grandma keeps trying to introduce him to nice girls, but he's a **confirmed bachelor**.
items.watchOut: «Переконаний холостяк» — confirmed bachelor; persuaded тут не підходить, а convinced bachelor звучить незвично. Про жінку старе confirmed spinster сьогодні звучить образливо; краще сказати she's happily single.

items.pattern: verb + noun: start a family (= have your first child)
items.meaning: have your first baby
items.example: When are you two going to **start a family**? — Mum, please stop asking!
more: Now that they've **started a family**, they rarely go out at night.
Lots of my friends **started a family** in their twenties.
items.watchOut: Start a family — народити першу дитину, а не «створити сім'ю» в сенсі «одружитися» (це get married). І не begin / create a family.

items.pattern: verb + noun: have children / kids
items.meaning: become a parent
items.example: My grandparents **had six children**, and all of them still live in the same town.
more: Not everyone wants to **have kids**, and that's fine.
They **have two children**: a boy at university and a girl at school.
items.watchOut: «Мати дітей», «завести дітей» — have children, а не get children і не make children.

items.pattern: verb + noun: be expecting a baby · be expecting (no object) · be expecting twins
items.meaning: be pregnant
items.example: My boss is **expecting a baby**, so she's going on maternity leave in June.
more: Kate looks tired; she's **expecting** her third child.
They found out they were **expecting** twins at the first scan.
items.watchOut: «Чекати дитину» — be expecting (a baby), а не wait (for) a baby: wait for — просто чекати, поки щось станеться чи хтось прийде.

items.pattern: verb + noun: have a baby (= give birth) · She had her baby on Monday
items.meaning: give birth to a baby
items.example: Anna **had her baby** on New Year's Day, so he'll always have a party on his birthday.
more: She's going to **have the baby** in the local hospital.
Women in my family usually **have their babies** quite young.
items.watchOut: «Народити» — have a baby або give birth (to), а не get a baby. «Я народився» — I was born.

items.pattern: noun + be + adjective: the baby is due (in May / next week) · she's due in May · a due date
items.meaning: the baby is expected to be born at that time
items.example: The **baby is due** in May, so they're painting the spare room now.
more: When is the **baby due**?
My sister is **due** next week and can't stop cleaning the flat.
items.watchOut: Due — «очікується за планом». Due date — передбачувана дата пологів. Порівняй: The train is due at six — потяг має прибути о шостій.

items.pattern: adjective + noun: a single parent / mother / father · a single-parent family
items.meaning: a person who brings up a child alone, without a partner
items.example: My dad was a **single father** for ten years before he met my stepmum.
more: The new nursery offers cheaper places for **single parents**.
She raised two boys as a **single mother** and still finished university.
items.watchOut: «Мати-одиначка» — single mother / single parent, а не lonely mother: lonely — самотній у значенні «сумно без людей». У Британії в офіційних текстах ще кажуть lone parent, а sole parent там зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: verb + noun: bring up / raise children / a family · bring sb up · be brought up by sb · raise a family is more US
items.meaning: look after children until they are adults and teach them how to behave
items.example: My parents **brought us up** to always say thank you.
more: Ten years of **raising a family** taught her more than any job.
She was **brought up** to believe that hard work always pays off.
items.watchOut: «Виховувати, виростити дитину» — bring up або raise a child, а не grow up a child (grow up — рости самому: I grew up in Lviv) і не educate (давати освіту). Із займенником: bring them up, а не bring up them.

items.pattern: verb + noun: apply for custody of sb · get / win / lose custody
items.meaning: officially ask a court for the right to look after a child after the parents separate
items.uk: звернутися до суду, щоб дитина жила з тобою; просити про опіку
items.example: Mark **applied for custody of** the children because he works from home and can look after them.
more: She's going to **apply for custody**, but her lawyer says it could take months.
In the end he got **custody** of the dog as well as the kids.
items.watchOut: Custody — право опіки: з ким житиме дитина після розлучення. Прийменники: apply for custody of the children. Не плутай: in police custody — під вартою.

items.pattern: verb + noun: give / grant (formal) custody (of sb) to sb · be granted custody · also award custody
items.meaning: (of a court or judge) officially decide which person will look after a child
items.uk: надати опіку, залишити дитину з кимось (рішення суду)
items.example: Thirty years ago, judges almost always **gave custody** to the mother.
more: Lawyers say it's rare for a court to **grant custody** to a parent who lives abroad.
Do you think the judge will **give her custody**?
items.watchOut: Grant — офіційніше слово, ним кажуть про рішення суду. У пасиві: She was granted custody (of the children).

items.pattern: verb + preposition + noun: provide for your family / children · compare provide sb with sth
items.meaning: earn enough money to pay for everything your family needs
items.example: After the factory closed, Oleh did all kinds of odd jobs to **provide for his family**.
more: When his dad got ill, sixteen-year-old Max had to help **provide for** his younger brothers.
He's always **provided for** us, even when times were hard.
items.watchOut: «Утримувати сім'ю» — provide for your family, з for. Без for (provide your family) — помилка; provide sb with sth — дати комусь щось: provide the kids with lunch. Ще кажуть support your family.

items.pattern: verb + noun: set up home (together / on your own) · usually no article
items.meaning: start living in your own house or flat, independent of your parents
items.example: My grandparents **set up home** in a tiny room in a shared flat in the 1960s.
more: They **set up home** together after just six months.
It's expensive to **set up home** in London these days.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай без артикля і без my: set up home, а не set up my home. Build a home частіше означає «збудувати будинок» буквально.

warmup.uk: Ми плануємо завести дітей після весілля.
warmup.q: We're planning to ___ a family after the wedding.
warmup.explain: Завести дітей — start a family. А «створити сім'ю» в сенсі «одружитися» — get married, не create a family.

warmup.uk: Моя сестра чекає дитину й уже вибирає імена.
warmup.q: My sister is ___ a baby, and she's already choosing names.
warmup.explain: Бути вагітною — be expecting a baby. Wait (for) — просто чекати, поки щось станеться.

warmup.uk: Бабусі й дідусі часто допомагають виховувати дітей, коли батьки працюють.
warmup.q: Grandparents often help to ___ the children when both parents work.
warmup.explain: Виховувати дітей — bring up або raise. Grow up — рости самому; grow — вирощувати рослини.

warmup.uk: Мама Олени і мій тато — двоюрідні, тож ми з Оленою — троюрідні сестри.
warmup.q: Olena's mum and my dad are cousins, so Olena and I are ___ cousins.
warmup.explain: Двоюрідні — first cousins, троюрідні — second cousins. Рахунок зсунутий на одиницю.
Покійний — late: his late wife. «Помер» ввічливо — passed away, але passed wife не кажуть.
Переконаний холостяк — a confirmed bachelor. Persuaded — «якого переконали», це про інше.

warmup.uk: Вона виросла в неповній сім'ї: її виховувала тільки мама.
warmup.q: She grew up in a ___-parent family: her mum brought her up alone.
warmup.explain: Сім'я з одним із батьків — a single-parent family, мати-одиначка — a single mother. Lonely — самотній у значенні «сумно без людей».

warmup.uk: У мене багато далеких родичів у Польщі.
warmup.q: I have a lot of ___ relatives in Poland.
warmup.explain: Далекі родичі — distant relatives. Far relatives так не кажуть.

A.q: My grandmother's cousin's son is a ___ relative of mine.
A.explain: Далекий родич — distant relative. Far relative так не кажуть.

A.q: The hotel was full of ___ families: doctors, lawyers and teachers on holiday with their children.
A.explain: Respectable — порядний, з добрим ім'ям. Respectful — шанобливий, той, хто сам виявляє повагу.

A.q: Every year on his birthday, we take flowers to the grave of my ___ grandfather.
A.explain: Покійний — late: my late grandfather. Passed тут не підходить: кажуть he passed away.

B.q: My parents waited ten years before they decided to ___ a family.
B.explain: Start a family — завести дітей. Make / begin a family так не кажуть.

B.q: Olha has given up coffee because she's ___ a baby.
B.explain: Бути вагітною — be expecting a baby. Waiting a baby — калька.

B.q: Tom ___ his twin daughters on his own after his wife left.
B.explain: Виховати дітей — bring up (або raise) children. Grow up — рости самому: I grew up in Odesa.

example.title: The family tree
example.uk:
Для шкільного проєкту моя донька вирішила намалювати наше родинне дерево. Вона почала з найближчої родини: з мене, мого чоловіка і свого молодшого брата. У нас дружна сім'я, тож усі наші дні народження вона знала напам'ять. Потім вона зателефонувала бабусі, щоб дізнатися про всю нашу велику рідню.

Виявилося, що в нас десятки далеких родичів у Канаді, зокрема троюрідна сестра, схожа на мене як дві краплі води. Бабуся розповіла про свого покійного чоловіка, який працював на двох роботах, щоб утримувати сім'ю, і допомагав їй виховувати чотирьох дітей.

Остання гілка належала дядькові Тому. Усі вважали його переконаним холостяком, але минулого місяця він одружився, і тепер його дружина чекає дитину. Дерево росте!
example.en:
For a school project, my daughter decided to draw our family tree. She started with our [[immediate family|a6]]: me, my husband and her little brother. We're a [[close-knit family|a8]], so she knew all our birthdays by heart. Then she phoned her grandmother to learn about our [[extended family|a2]].

It turned out we have dozens of [[distant relatives|a4]] in Canada, including a [[second cousin|a5]] who looks just like me. Grandma talked about her [[late husband|a12]], who worked two jobs to [[provide for his family|b10]] and helped her [[bring up|b7]] four children.

The last branch was Uncle Tom's. Everyone thought he was a [[confirmed bachelor|a21]], but last month he got married, and now his wife is [[expecting a baby|b3]]. The tree is growing!
